_comment: Spots permanently excluded from the surf-spot database. Matched by exact name against the candidate/enriched records. Grouped by reason for reviewability. great_lakes: freshwater Great Lakes spots that were carrying ocean WFO tags and validated FAR at 402-550 km as domain misses, because the pipeline fetched an Atlantic grid and looked for them hundreds of km inland. NOAA DOES run NWPS for Great Lakes WFOs, so these could in principle be served by retagging, but the swell-window and raycast model assumes distant swell propagation while Great Lakes surf is short-fetch wind sea that dies within hours of the wind dropping. Serving them properly is a separate project, not a retag. Excluded rather than deleted so the decision is recorded and a future seed rebuild does not reintroduce them. SECOND BATCH, found by a different route: these fourteen carried NO nwps_wfo tag at all rather than a wrong one, because the WFO assignment step maps ocean coastlines only, so a freshwater spot receives nothing - the enrichment behaving correctly, not failing. The rationale above is unchanged and applies to them identically. Every untagged spot in spots_enriched.json turned out to be freshwater Great Lakes, so after this batch the untagged set is EMPTY: an absent nwps_wfo is no longer a state any record is in. duplicates: a spot already present in the database under its correct name. Boyton Bech Inlet is a MISSPELLED duplicate of Boynton Beach Inlet, carried in the backlog since the project began. It survived because the misspelling gave it a distinct slug AND its nearest NWPS node was a different cell (26.548,-80.02792 against 26.512,-80.04765), so it would have PLACED as a separate spot rather than colliding with the real one - nothing in the pipeline would have flagged it. Excluded when the mfl backlog was finally placed. St Andews Park and Cape San B liss are the same failure with a different origin: commit 9674d67 corrected both misspellings in spots_enriched.json, which changed their DERIVED slugs (st-andews-park to st-andrews-park, cape-san-b-liss to cape-san-blas). db_import upserts on slug, so the corrected records inserted as new rows while the old rows were left behind - nothing deletes a row whose slug stopped being produced. The orphans then went stale: import_forecasts joins ratings.json by NAME, and no ratings entry carries the misspelling any more, so they stopped receiving source=nwps rows entirely, while ecmwf_wam kept writing to them because it joins on the spots table's own id and never looks at names. Excluded by the PRE-RENAME names, which is what the orphan rows still hold; the live replacements st-andrews-park and cape-san-blas must survive and are deliberately NOT listed here.
